2501856e66ad2c94f1f1.text: This module was made to help you understand your grammar lesson about

4aa0090e407f965e0067.text: conditionals more. It is made for you to be able to express arguments using zero, first, second and third conditionals. The scope of this module allows you to use what you have learned from your previous lessons about conditionals and enables you to use it in different real-life situation.

99aad8be3cb029a7ad3c.text: After going through this module, you are expected to: 1. Recognize the different types of conditional sentences (zero, first, second

2c6f5895783298b9403c.text: and third); 2. Use the correct structure for each type of conditional; 3. Determine the idea expressed by a conditional statement; and 4. Compose an argumentative essay that demonstrates the appropriate use of conditional statements.

bc48a6bc240d25800c85.text: I. Directions: Choose the letter of the correct form of the verb in each conditional sentence.

e8c7f1e5241a6cf7ab7a.text: If you heat water to 100°, it _____________. a.

6014c6715efe4ec8761e.text: If opportunity knocks, _____________ the door. a.

5935711ab9b5a7bc52b1.text: If you go at this hour, you _____________ traffic. a.

57fc5b363a5756fd5069.text: You worked hard today. But if you rest, you _____________ better. a.

3b8d64389693eea5293e.text: If you set your mind to a goal, soon you _____________ it. a.

38dea425e548e7361a01.text: If I had more time, I _____________ one more book. a.

9fdf5bd4b759c6599a47.text: If I were president, I _____________ some changes for our country. a.

d1533f3075365eb1ee9f.text: If you had been a good example, I _____________ to you. a.

6a1b0e7b675f06c9a3ce.text: If we had left earlier, we _____________ on time. a.

50a25fc807d6263cc680.text: 10. If you wash your hands often, you _____________ colds.

e0e86eb08397330ceac0.text: Directions: Match the type of conditionals in column

79b923ed3b739fd1aa29.text: A with its correct definition in Column B.

rows: This conditional sentence is used to explain that present circumstances would be different if something different had happened in the past.
This conditional sentence is used to express situations in which the outcome is likely (but not guaranteed) to happen in the future.
This conditional sentence expresses general truths or situations in which one thing always causes another.
This conditional sentence is useful for expressing outcomes that are completely unrealistic or will not likely happen in the future.
2de28becc78858ae4730.text: A  B  1. Zero Conditional A This conditional sentence is used to explain that present circumstances would be different if something different had happened in the past. 2. First Conditional B This conditional sentence is used to express situations in which the outcome is likely (but not guaranteed) to happen in the future. 3. Second Conditional C This conditional sentence expresses general truths or situations in which one thing always causes another. 4. Third Conditional D This conditional sentence is useful for expressing outcomes that are completely unrealistic or will not likely happen in the future.

0a4c42fef9ba5de701ea.text: Using Conditionals (Zero, First, Second and Third

bed2353595edecc36da4.text: In your previous lessons, you have learned about conditionals and its type

5526460ef6888375a547.text: and usage. As a review, a Conditional sentence is a type of sentence that expresses a condition and the outcome or the result of that condition. A condition is something that can occur IF something else happens.

289c00b513afe8978ae9.text: A Conditional sentence is of a dependent clause and an independent clause

e4cd587bc29f9d3a871f.text: that are put together to express the condition and the result.

edaad6f7fbeb1a977db2.text: If you stay at home, you will be safer from the threat of the pandemic.

755a9804ab1c0ead0e65.text: The if-clause tells you the condition (If you stay at home) and the main clause tells you the result (you will be safer from the threat of the pandemic).

460fb824ba795b542597.text: We use the zero conditional to talk about things about general truth, especially for laws and rules.

87aa5eb8cf49953c668e.text: We use the first conditional when we talk about the future situation that is possible to happen or can happen in reality.

9f5e53936d7d73e0cc46.text: The second conditional is used to express the present or future situation that is impossible or unlikely to happen in reality.

19851fa2b91d13bef275.text: The third conditional is used to refer to a time that is in the pastor unreal past condition and express its probable past result.

058f54980da2ba7cbcbe.text: Conditional sentences are also used to express arguments. Arguments are

51130095cdfa502d0665.text: statements expressing a reason or set of reasons given to persuade others that a certain action or given idea is right or wrong. It is also used to deliver or to present a reason or reasons why you support or oppose an idea or suggestion.

b2eeb459ddff93f84787.text: In expressing arguments using conditional sentences, you are going to present

46d437c2d0f515c408a8.text: your response as the result from a given condition (if-clause) and/or you will tell the possible or the probable cause of a certain situation or result (main-clause).

1443a0a9a071bb013d4d.text: Situation: Mary’s teacher sent a reminder in their class’ group chat that the

d8e0d43aad5b4fb87bbe.text: submission of their module would be on the day after next. John, one of her classmates, asked her to send him her answer because he forgot to work on his module. If you were Mary, would you help John finish his module by sending him your answers? Why or why not?

183d6f2c5f0e42b61c3f.text: Possible Answer: If I were Mary, I would help John finish his module, but I would not

36749f3f7c17d4c2aeb0.text: send him my answers. I would tell him to start doing his module now and help him out in understanding the lesson. I would also motivate him to answer his module ahead of time so he would not cram the night before the submission.

30955b3b14e03b598bc9.text: Make sure to use the correct type of conditional based on the form/tense of

523c32ac84e138de8fee.text: the verb given on the question/situation.

ef64dbfddc422f7fbe7e.text: A. Directions: Read the text below entitled “Thank you Ma’am” by Langston Hughes

acaf1516a2eb0af6b84e.text: and reflect on the questions that you will encounter as you read.

765c71d37caccd36b99f.text: She was a large woman with a large purse that had everything in it but

dc86d19e1d79b82270e7.text: hammer and nails. It had a long strap, and she carried it slung across her shoulder. It was about eleven o’clock at night, and she was walking alone, when a boy ran up behind her and tried to snatch her purse. The strap broke with the single tug the boy gave it from behind. But the boy’s weight and the weight of the purse combined caused him to lose his balance so, instead of taking off full blast as he had hoped, the boy fell on his back on the sidewalk, and his legs flew up. The large woman simply turned around and kicked him right square in his blue-jeaned sitter. Then she reached down, picked the boy up by his shirt front, and shook him until his teeth rattled.

b6ad4fe6043614dfcf58.text: After that the woman said, “Pick up my pocketbook, boy, and give it here.”

a292b71ca2c6c6166b96.text: She still held him. But she bent down enough to permit him to stoop and pick up her purse.

ead9c11eb6b83f98ba4b.text: Then she said, “Now ain’t you ashamed of yourself?” Firmly gripped by his shirt front, the boy said, “Yes’m.” The woman said, “What did you want to do it for?” The boy said, “I didn’t aim to.” She said, “You a lie!” By that time two or three people passed, stopped, turned to look, and some

25dc54ae74d0c10d68e4.text: “If I turn you loose, will you run?” asked the woman. “Yes’m,” said the boy. “Then I won’t turn you loose,” said the woman. She did not release him. “I’m

ec0544d9ce68da8acf06.text: very sorry, lady, I’m sorry,” whispered the boy.

c7dcf52e66d634c4aff8.text: “Um-hum! And your face is dirty. I got a great mind to wash your face for you. Ain’t you got nobody home to tell you to wash your face?” “No’m,” said the boy. “Then it will get washed this evening,” said the large woman starting up the

a3c47f246936d0d43634.text: street, dragging the frightened boy behind her.

96fcd116eb09ab4dbe60.text: He looked as if he were fourteen or fifteen, frail and willow-wild, in tennis

77f0da445c4f6677ea89.text: shoes and blue jeans. The woman said, “You ought to be my son. I would teach you right from wrong. Least I can do right now is to wash your face. Are you hungry?”

b9c1d6510b8bfc3f93e6.text: If you were Roger, would you trust Mrs. Jones right away?

759c64883680993d9f42.text: “No’m,” said the being dragged boy. “I just want you to turn me loose.” “Was I

95b2b49142e2325b6328.text: bothering you when I turned that corner?” asked the woman.

bd458014163e86876e28.text: “No’m.” “But you put yourself in contact with me,” said the woman. “If you think that

867fc066faaa45a1cff2.text: that contact is not going to last awhile, you got another thought coming. When I get through with you, sir, you are going to remember Mrs. Luella Bates Washington Jones.”

0ff9b4811f650b163e7e.text: Sweat popped out on the boy’s face and he began to struggle. Mrs. Jones

2fd993435f06df9cd9ee.text: stopped, jerked him around in front of her, put a half-nelson about his neck, and continued to drag him up the street. When she got to her door, she dragged the boy inside, down a hall, and into a large kitchenette- furnished room at the rear of the house. She switched on the light and left the door open. The boy could hear other roomers laughing and talking in the large house. Some of their doors were open, too, so he knew he and the woman were not alone. The woman still had him by the neck in the middle of her room.

1464000b061f4f5b8140.text: She said, “What is your name?” “Roger,” answered the boy. “Then, Roger, you go to that sink and wash your face,” said the woman,

6ae0ab4f234ee1aa688f.text: whereupon she turned him loose—at last. Roger looked at the door—looked at the woman—looked at the door—and went to the sink.

4988945239727bed4594.text: Let the water run until it gets warm,” she said. “Here’s a clean towel.” “You

937b9c98807c578c7665.text: gonna take me to jail?” asked the boy, bending over the sink.

03ec55e158e4e5f53d88.text: “Not with that face, I would not take you nowhere,” said the woman. “Here I

91441aa139f03e11e1bb.text: am trying to get home to cook me a bite to eat, and you snatch my pocketbook! Maybe, you ain’t been to your supper either, late as it be. Have you?”

bd498a4ec9c9d99a9e79.text: “There’s nobody home at my house,” said the boy. “Then we’ll eat,” said the woman, “I believe you’re hungry—or been hungry—

3d9c5c3597dd30a63871.text: to try to snatch my pocketbook.”

493c0b6b6c2fafaba4b6.text: “I wanted a pair of blue suede shoes,” said the boy. “Well, you didn’t have to snatch my pocketbook to get some suede shoes,” said

82f26da6acf78aad74ca.text: Mrs. Luella Bates Washington Jones. “You could of asked me.”

8492a9a15c903d8a376c.text: “M’am?” The water dripping from his face, the boy looked at her. There was a long

2d6e592342374dca8d1b.text: pause. A very long pause. After he had dried his face and not knowing what else to do dried it again, the boy turned around, wondering what next. The door was open. He could make a dash for it down the hall. He could run, run, run, run, run!

b7f78c10c2f35702cf9e.text: If you were Roger, would you run?

dd1358da42bf6ed359a8.text: The woman was sitting on the daybed. After a while she said, “I were young

0dacd8d03e782a5b444d.text: once and I wanted things I could not get.”

76e38981096259cf6155.text: There was another long pause. The boy’s mouth opened. Then he frowned, but

0bffb48dfec26157748f.text: The woman said, “Um-hum! You thought I was going to say but, didn’t you?

3ba6bce678d805c83f76.text: You thought I was going to say, but I didn’t snatch people’s pocketbooks. Well, I wasn’t going to say that.” Pause. Silence. “I have done things, too, which I would not tell you, son—neither tell God, if he didn’t already know. So, you set down while I fix us something to eat. You might run that comb through your hair so you will look presentable.”

0395aadbe2654f7c3468.text: What did Roger feel at this moment?

d78f3c15c96c1c8b04b9.text: In another corner of the room behind a screen was a gas plate and an icebox.

6eafe48a60b01b2a80c8.text: Mrs. Jones got up and went behind the screen. The woman did not watch the boy to see if he was going to run now, nor did she watch her purse which she left behind her on the daybed. But the boy took care to sit on the far side of the room where he thought she could easily see him out of the corner of her eye, if she wanted to. He did not trust the woman not to trust him. And he did not want to be mistrusted now.

9cef12e604698df9465b.text: “Do you need somebody to go to the store,” asked the boy, “maybe to get some

ec22b3b52c7f66d178a9.text: “Don’t believe I do,” said the woman, “unless you just want sweet milk

41641d06855018008e52.text: yourself. I was going to make cocoa out of this canned milk I got here.” “That will be fine,” said the boy.

f88ef7ac2fc157691d03.text: She heated some lima beans and ham she had in the icebox, made the cocoa,

835550fb067f28431641.text: and set the table. The woman did not ask the boy anything about where he lived, or his folks, or anything else that would embarrass him.

7ffa235a9a69b3d99467.text: Instead, as they ate, she told him about her job in a hotel beauty-shop that

729946f5ea29eb58c6ae.text: stayed open late, what the work was like, and how all kinds of women came in and out, blondes, red-heads, and Spanish. Then she cut him a half of her ten-cent cake.

ecaa44bbe1f501b5dcd3.text: “Eat some more, son,” she said. When they were finished eating, she got up and said, “Now, here, take these

ca93ba3ec7e5d38b948a.text: ten dollars and buy yourself some blue suede shoes. And next time, do not make the mistake of latching onto my pocketbook nor nobody else’s— because shoes come by devilish like that will burn your feet. I got to get my rest now. But I wish you would behave yourself, son, from here on in.”

40f43595addfd6aa407d.text: Remember the most recent act of kindness you did for someone. Why

dbb92753e27e67536b0d.text: She led him down the hall to the front door and opened it. “Goodnight! Behave

b22a13a0a4581ff12a77.text: yourself, boy!” she said, looking out into the street. The boy wanted to say something else other than “Thank you, m’am” to Mrs. Luella Bates Washington Jones, but he couldn’t do so as he turned at the barren stoop and looked back at the large woman in the door. He barely managed to say “Thank you” before she shut the door. And he never saw her again.

15f2d011bf71348fdce6.text: B. Directions: Answer the following questions. 1. How did Mrs. Jones react when Roger had tried to steal her purse?

d6a385b34563b438402f.text: 2. Was her reaction believable? Why or why not?

9bfd56985d623759d9fe.text: 5. Do you think Roger’s encounter with Mrs. Jones altered his life? In what way?

9a863584d6957f67be60.text: 6. Why did Hughes title the story, Thank You, Ma’am?

e8b4436d679ea56c5fb5.text: 7. In what way did the characters show what they had accomplished at the end of the story?

685df0d417c8886f26f9.text: 2. You should ______________ your nose and mouth if you sneeze. a. cover

If Roger continues to steal things from people, _____________________________. a. he will be successful. b. he would have ended in jail. c. he would have reached his dreams. d. he will regret his wrongdoing in the future.

10112bfd5e69b12a9b9c.text: 7. If you had waited for the right time, _____________________________. a. you will be tired. b. having patience is not for you. c. you will not find the things for you. d. the reward of waiting would have been priceless.

If you had been in her shoes, what are the things you would have done? a. If I had been in her shoes, I would not care at all. b. If I had been in her shoes, I would have done the same thing. c. If I am asked to give advice to my younger cousins on how to avoid getting sick, I will tell them to have it researched on the internet. c. If I am asked to give advice to my younger cousins on how to avoid getting sick, I will tell them that they will learn about it from school so they will be excited. d.
